Step 3:Data Preprocessing
```{r}
# Create a preprocessing function
preprocess_data <- function(data) {
  
  # 1. Handle target variable
  df_clean <- data %>%
    mutate(FraudFound = ifelse(FraudFound == "Yes", 1, 0))
  
  # 2. Remove identifier columns that don't add predictive value
  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    select(-PolicyNumber)  # Remove policy number if it exists
  
  # 3. Handle missing values
  # For numeric columns: impute with median
  numeric_cols <- df_clean %>% select_if(is.numeric) %>% names()
  for(col in numeric_cols) {
    df_clean[[col]][is.na(df_clean[[col]])] <- median(df_clean[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  
  # For categorical columns: impute with mode or create "Unknown" category
  categorical_cols <- df_clean %>% select_if(is.character) %>% names()
  for(col in categorical_cols) {
    if(any(is.na(df_clean[[col]]))) {
      df_clean[[col]][is.na(df_clean[[col]])] <- "Unknown"
    }
  }
  
  return(df_clean)
}

# Apply preprocessing
df_clean <- preprocess_data(data=df)
df_clean
```

Step 4:Feature Engineering
```{r}
feature_engineering <- function(data) {
  
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(
      # Monetary anomaly: Claim amount relative to vehicle value
      claim_to_value_ratio = ClaimAmount / VehiclePrice,
      
      # Behavioral velocity: Claims per year (if you have policy tenure)
       claims_per_year = PastNumberOfClaims / PolicyTenure,
      
      # Temporal features
       claim_month = as.factor(Month),
       claim_day = as.factor(DayOfWeek),
      
      # Risk score combination
      high_risk_combo = ifelse(PastNumberOfClaims > 2 & 
                                 DriverRating < 3, 1, 0),
      
      # Vehicle age category
      vehicle_age_cat = case_when(
        AgeOfVehicle <= 3 ~ "New",
        AgeOfVehicle <= 7 ~ "Medium",
        TRUE ~ "Old"
      )
    )
  
  return(data)
}

df_engineered <- feature_engineering(df_clean)
df_engineered
```

Step 5:Encode Categorical Variables
```{r}
# Load required library for creating dummy variables
library(fastDummies)
# Make sure we have the data
df_engineered <- feature_engineering(df_clean)

# IDENTIFYING ALL COLUMN TYPES FIRST
str(df_engineered)

# SEPARATING TARGET FROM FEATURES
# Ensuring FraudFound is numeric (0/1)
df_model <- df_engineered %>%
  mutate(FraudFound = ifelse(FraudFound == "Yes" | FraudFound == 1, 1, 0))

# Store target separately
y <- df_model$FraudFound

# Remove target and any ID columns from features
X <- df_model %>%
  select(-FraudFound, -any_of(c("PolicyNumber", "policy_id", "RowID")))

# 1. Identify column types
numeric_cols <- X %>% select_if(is.numeric) %>% names()
character_cols <- X %>% select_if(is.character) %>% names()
factor_cols <- X %>% select_if(is.factor) %>% names()

cat("Numeric columns:", length(numeric_cols), "\n")
cat("Character columns:", length(character_cols), "\n")
cat("Factor columns:", length(factor_cols), "\n")

# 2. Convert character columns to factors first
X_processed <- X
if(length(character_cols) > 0) {
  X_processed <- X_processed %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(character_cols), as.factor))
}

# 3. NOW create dummy variables for ALL categorical columns (factors)
if(length(factor_cols) > 0 || length(character_cols) > 0) {
  # Get all factor columns after conversion
  all_factor_cols <- X_processed %>% select_if(is.factor) %>% names()
  
  # Create dummy variables
  X_encoded <- dummy_cols(
    X_processed,
    select_columns = all_factor_cols,
    remove_first_dummy = TRUE,  # Avoids multicollinearity
    remove_selected_columns = TRUE  # Removes original categorical columns
  )
} else {
  X_encoded <- X_processed
}

# 4. To ensure ALL columns are numeric
X_numeric <- X_encoded %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))

# 5. To check for any remaining non-numeric or infinite values
str(X_numeric)
summary(X_numeric)

# 6. To handle any NA/NaN/Inf values
X_numeric <- X_numeric %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ifelse(is.na(.) | is.nan(.) | is.infinite(.), 0, .)))

# 7. Convert to matrix
X_matrix <- as.matrix(X_numeric)

# Verifying there are no issues
cat("Matrix dimensions:", dim(X_matrix), "\n")
cat("Matrix class:", class(X_matrix), "\n")
cat("First few values:\n")
print(X_matrix[1:3, 1:5])
```

Step 6: Handle Class Imbalance with SMOTE
```{r}
library(smotefamily)

# SMOTE requires data frame, not matrix
X_df <- as.data.frame(X_matrix)

# Applying SMOTE
set.seed(123)
smote_result <- SMOTE(X = X_df, 
                      target = as.numeric(y), 
                      K = 5)

# Extracting balanced data
X_balanced <- smote_result$data[, -ncol(smote_result$data)]
y_balanced <- smote_result$data$class

# Converting back to matrix (ensuring numeric)
X_balanced_matrix <- as.matrix(X_balanced)
storage.mode(X_balanced_matrix) <- "numeric"  # Force numeric storage

# Verifying there is no error
cat("Balanced data dimensions:", dim(X_balanced_matrix), "\n")
cat("Class distribution:\n")
table(y_balanced)
```



Step 7: Split Data into Training and Testing Sets
```{r}
# Splitting the balanced data
set.seed(42)
train_index <- createDataPartition(y_balanced, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)

X_train <- X_balanced_matrix[train_index, , drop = FALSE]
X_test  <- X_balanced_matrix[-train_index, , drop = FALSE]

y_train <- y_balanced[train_index]
y_test  <- y_balanced[-train_index]

# CHANGING EVERYTHING TO NUMERIC
X_train <- apply(X_train, 2, as.numeric)
X_test  <- apply(X_test, 2, as.numeric)

y_train <- as.numeric(y_train)
y_test  <- as.numeric(y_test)

# Replacing problematic values
X_train[is.na(X_train)] <- 0
X_test[is.na(X_test)] <- 0

X_train[is.infinite(X_train)] <- 0
X_test[is.infinite(X_test)] <- 0

# Convert to matrix explicitly
X_train <- as.matrix(X_train)
X_test  <- as.matrix(X_test)

# Verifying types
print(class(X_train))
print(class(X_test))
print(typeof(X_train))

# Creating DMatrix
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train, label = y_train)
dtest  <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test, label = y_test)

cat("DMatrix successfully created!\n")
```
Step 8: Set XGBoost Parameters
```{r}
# Set parameters for binary classification
params <- list(
  objective = "binary:logistic",
  eval_metric = c("auc","logloss"),
  max_depth = 6,
  eta = 0.1,
  subsample = 0.8,
  colsample_bytree = 0.8,
  min_child_weight = 1,
  gamma = 0,
  scale_pos_weight = 1
)
```

Step 9: Train the XGBoost Model with Cross-Validation
```{r}
# Perform cross-validation to find optimal number of rounds
set.seed(123)

xgb_cv <- xgb.cv(
  params = params,
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = 1000,
  nfold = 5,
  early_stopping_rounds = 50,
  verbose = 1,
  maximize = TRUE     # AUC must be maximized
)
#Ploting Cross-Validation Results
cv_log <- xgb_cv$evaluation_log

plot(cv_log$iter, cv_log$test_auc_mean,
     type = "l", col = "blue",
     xlab = "Number of rounds",
     ylab = "AUC",
     main = "Cross-Validation AUC")

lines(cv_log$iter, cv_log$train_auc_mean, col = "red")

legend("bottomright",
       legend = c("Test AUC", "Train AUC"),
       col = c("blue","red"),
       lty = 1)
#Get Optimal Number of Rounds
best_nrounds <- xgb_cv$best_iteration
cat("Best number of rounds:", best_nrounds, "\n")
# Check best iteration from CV
best_nrounds <- xgb_cv$best_iteration

# Fallback if best_nrounds is NULL
if(is.null(best_nrounds) || best_nrounds <= 0){
  cat("best_nrounds is invalid, setting to default 100\n")
  best_nrounds <- 100
} else {
  cat("Best number of rounds from CV:", best_nrounds, "\n")
}

# Training the final model
xgb_model <- xgb.train(
  params = params,
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = best_nrounds,
  watchlist = list(train = dtrain, test = dtest),
  verbose = 1,
  maximize = TRUE  # ensures metrics like AUC are maximized
)
```
Step 10: Hyperparameter Tuning
```{r}
library(doParallel)
library(foreach)
# Register cores
registerDoParallel(cores = 4)

# Parameter grid
param_grid <- expand.grid(
  max_depth = c(4,6,8),
  eta = c(0.01,0.1,0.3),
  subsample = c(0.7,0.8,0.9),
  colsample_bytree = c(0.7,0.8,0.9)
)

# Grid search using parallel processing
results <- foreach(
  i = 1:nrow(param_grid),
  .combine = rbind,
  .packages = "xgboost",
  .export = c("X_train","y_train")
) %dopar% {

  # Recreate DMatrix INSIDE worker
  dtrain_local <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train, label = y_train)

  params <- list(
    objective = "binary:logistic",
    eval_metric = "auc",
    max_depth = param_grid$max_depth[i],
    eta = param_grid$eta[i],
    subsample = param_grid$subsample[i],
    colsample_bytree = param_grid$colsample_bytree[i]
  )

  cv <- xgb.cv(
    params = params,
    data = dtrain_local,
    nrounds = 500,
    nfold = 3,
    early_stopping_rounds = 20,
    verbose = 0,
    maximize = TRUE
  )

  auc <- max(cv$evaluation_log$test_auc_mean)

  data.frame(param_grid[i,], auc = auc)
}

# Best parameters
best_params <- results[which.max(results$auc),]

print(best_params)
```


Step 11: Make Predictions and Evaluate
```{r}
# Predict on test set
predictions <- predict(xgb_model, dtest)

# Convert probabilities to binary predictions (threshold = 0.5)
predicted_classes <- ifelse(predictions > 0.5, 1, 0)

# Confusion matrix
confusionMatrix(as.factor(predicted_classes), as.factor(y_test))

# Calculate metrics
# Precision, Recall, F1 Score
precision <- posPredValue(as.factor(predicted_classes), as.factor(y_test))
recall <- sensitivity(as.factor(predicted_classes), as.factor(y_test))
f1 <- (2 * precision * recall) / (precision + recall)

cat("Precision:", precision, "\n")
cat("Recall:", recall, "\n")
cat("F1 Score:", f1, "\n")

# ROC Curve and AUC
pred <- prediction(predictions, y_test)
perf <- performance(pred, "tpr", "fpr")
plot(perf, col = "blue", main = "ROC Curve")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "gray")

auc <- performance(pred, "auc")@y.values[[1]]
cat("AUC:", auc, "\n")

# Precision-Recall curve (as mentioned in your proposal)
pr_perf <- performance(pred, "prec", "rec")
plot(pr_perf, col = "blue", main = "Precision-Recall Curve")
```

Step 13: Threshold Optimization for Fraud Detection
```{r}
# Find optimal threshold based on F1 score
thresholds <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.01)
f1_scores <- numeric(length(thresholds))

for(i in 1:length(thresholds)) {
  pred_class <- ifelse(predictions > thresholds[i], 1, 0)
  precision <- posPredValue(as.factor(pred_class), as.factor(y_test))
  recall <- sensitivity(as.factor(pred_class), as.factor(y_test))
  f1_scores[i] <- (2 * precision * recall) / (precision + recall)
}

optimal_threshold <- thresholds[which.max(f1_scores)]
cat("Optimal threshold:", optimal_threshold, "\n")

# Plot F1 vs threshold
plot(thresholds, f1_scores, type = "l", 
     xlab = "Threshold", ylab = "F1 Score",
     main = "F1 Score vs Threshold")
abline(v = optimal_threshold, col = "red", lty = 2)
```

STEP 15: Generate Out-of-Fold Predictions for Ensemble
```{r}
# Ensure the entire dataset is numeric BEFORE cross-validation
X_balanced_matrix <- as.matrix(X_balanced_matrix)
storage.mode(X_balanced_matrix) <- "numeric"

# Replace problematic values
X_balanced_matrix[is.na(X_balanced_matrix)] <- 0
X_balanced_matrix[is.infinite(X_balanced_matrix)] <- 0

# Ensure target is numeric
y_balanced <- as.numeric(y_balanced)

# Load model
xgb_model <- xgb.load("xgboost_fraud_model.json")

# Test predictions
xgb_test_predictions <- predict(xgb_model, dtest)

set.seed(456)
n_folds <- 5
folds <- createFolds(y_balanced, k = n_folds, list = TRUE)

# Initialize OOF predictions
xgb_oof_predictions <- numeric(length(y_balanced))

for(i in 1:n_folds){

  cat("Processing fold", i, "...\n")

  val_indices <- folds[[i]]
  train_indices <- setdiff(seq_along(y_balanced), val_indices)

  # Split data
  X_train_fold <- X_balanced_matrix[train_indices, , drop = FALSE]
  X_val_fold   <- X_balanced_matrix[val_indices, , drop = FALSE]

  y_train_fold <- y_balanced[train_indices]

  # Force numeric storage again (safety)
  storage.mode(X_train_fold) <- "numeric"
  storage.mode(X_val_fold) <- "numeric"

  # Create DMatrix
  dtrain_fold <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train_fold, label = y_train_fold)
  dval_fold   <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_val_fold)

  # Train model
  model_fold <- xgb.train(
    params = params,
    data = dtrain_fold,
    nrounds = best_nrounds,
    verbose = 0
  )

  # Predict validation fold
  xgb_oof_predictions[val_indices] <- predict(model_fold, dval_fold)
}

# Save predictions
saveRDS(xgb_oof_predictions, "xgb_oof_predictions.rds")
saveRDS(xgb_test_predictions, "xgb_test_predictions.rds")
saveRDS(y_balanced, "ensemble_target.rds")

cat("✓ Out-of-fold predictions saved for ensemble building\n")
```

Step 16: Allignment with original data
```{r}
# After generating xgb_oof_predictions on balanced data map back to original dataset indices

# Create mapping from balanced indices to original rows
original_indices <- which(y == 1 | y == 0)  
balanced_to_original <- rep(NA, length(y_balanced))

# For each balanced sample, track original index
balanced_to_original <- rep(NA, length(y_balanced))

# Assuming SMOTE keeps original rows first then adds synthetic
n_original <- length(y)
balanced_to_original[1:n_original] <- 1:n_original
# Synthetic rows get NA (will be removed later)

# Create aligned predictions
xgb_oof_aligned <- rep(NA, nrow(df))
xgb_oof_aligned[balanced_to_original[!is.na(balanced_to_original)]] <- 
  xgb_oof_predictions[!is.na(balanced_to_original)]

# Save aligned predictions
saveRDS(xgb_oof_aligned, "xgb_oof_aligned.rds")
```
